High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Akhilendra Singh - Government Advocate for the appe
 Shri Parmanand Sahu - Advocate for the respondent.

Order 
Per: Justice Atul Sreedharan Heard on Cr.A. No.7440/2019, where the State is aggrieved by the judgment passed by the learned trial Court only the quantum of sentence and that the appellant,
who has only been convicted for an offence under Section 376/511 IPC, should have been convicted for the offence under Section 3 & 4 POCSO Act and also Section 363 IPC.

2. The summary of facts of the case is that the prosecutrix aged about 7 years was taken away by the respondent in this case and he stated to have removed her clothes, his clothes and lay over her and committed the bad act.
The MLC of the prosecutrix, which is Ex.P/10, reflects that there were no signs of injury on the external part of the body of the prosecutrix and that her hymen was intact.

The Doctor also prepared two vaginal slides, which were NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:21362 2 CRA-7440-2019 sent to the FSL for testing.
The FSL report reflects that there was no human sperm on the vaginal slides though human sperm was found on the undergarments of the prosecutrix.
However, the said stains on the undergarments of the prosecutrix were never sent for DNA verification as it ought to have been done in order to connect the same with the respondent herein.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under the circumstances, there is no perversity in the judgment of the learned trial Court convicting the appellant for offence of attempt commit rape and imposing a sentence of 10 years,
which is also the punishment for attempt to commit an offence under the POSCO Act as per Section 5/9 read with Section 18 which provides for half the sentence for the offence of penetrative sexual assault.

4. Thus, as the material on record does not establish penetrative sexual assault, this Court is of opinion that the finding arrived by the trial Court is not perverse and the appellant has rightly been convicted only for an offence of attempt commit rape.
5. Thus, the appeal filed by the State is dismissed.
(ATUL SREEDHARAN) (ANURAD  JUDGE J  Shanu The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Deepak @ Pawan on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85057911/
